Install Orcacode

On macOS and Linux, one command installs the binary:

$ curl -fsSL https://orcapods.ai/orcacode.sh | sh

The installer detects your OS and architecture, downloads the matching release, verifies its SHA-256 checksum, and writes a single executable to ~/.local/bin. There is no runtime to install alongside it. If that directory is not on your PATH, the installer tells you how to add it.

On Windows, run the PowerShell installer:

> irm https://orcapods.ai/orcacode.ps1 | iex

Every build is also attached to the GitHub releases page with a SHA256SUMS file. orcacode update installs the latest release in place.

Environment variableUse it when
ORCACODE_VERSIONYou want to pin a release tag, for example orcacode-v0.7.0, instead of taking the latest.
ORCACODE_INSTALL_DIRYou want the binary somewhere other than ~/.local/bin.

To work on the harness itself rather than use it, build from a checkout with cargo run --release -p orcacode.

Your first prompt

Run orcacode from the workspace you want its file tools rooted in, or pass --workspace DIR to point them elsewhere.

$ orcacode

› Read the README and explain how this project is structured.
› Now identify the smallest test command for the CLI.

Use /help to open the command list. Type / to filter it. Press Esc to interrupt a running turn; prompts sent during a run are queued in order.

Useful launch options

OptionUse it when
--workspace DIRTools should be rooted in another directory.
--model NAMEYou know the model identifier to use.
--base-url URLYour compatible endpoint is not the default.
--openrouterYou want OpenRouter as the active endpoint.
--planYou want a read-first planning session.
--normalYou want to state the default human-approval mode explicitly.
--autoYou want guarded edits to proceed automatically and remaining risks reviewed.
--orchestrateYou want the agent to delegate substantial work while permitting basic direct edits.
--continueYou want the latest session for this workspace.
CHECK BEFORE YOU ACT

Normal mode is the default and asks before gated actions in the interactive terminal. --auto replaces those prompts with automatic admission and review; --yolo removes review entirely. Use plan mode when no state-changing action should run.
